summary: Keepalive connection-pool saturation triggers 5xx wave and runtime OOM/restart cycle
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-14 12:05 UTC customers (primarily a set of dedicated tenants) started seeing a sustained wave of 5xx responses for inference requests routed through the edge proxy. Impact: ~8% error rate on affected tenants, increased latency and several runtime containers entered OOM/restart cycles causing cascading 502/503 spikes. Environment: production (us-east-1), dedicated capacity cluster for NimbusPayments. Observed behavior: Edge/NGINX-style proxy connection pools became saturated with long-lived keepalive connections. Pool exhaustion caused head-of-line blocking in the proxy, which backed up request queues to upstream serving runtimes. The serving runtime began accumulating in-flight request state and KV cache entries until memory pressure triggered OOM kills and container restarts. Expected behavior: Keepalive should be bounded per-tenant and proxies should drop stalled connections before creating backpressure to upstream; autoscaler should add nodes before upstream OOMs occur.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Route sustained streaming workloads with many long-lived keepalive connections from a single tenant to the dedicated edge pool
2) Observe edge proxy keepalive connection count approaching configured max (observed ~95% of pool capacity),
3) See increased request queueing latencies at proxy and rising memory RSS on serving runtime pods,
4) After sustained pressure, runtime containers OOM and restart leading to 502/503 responses in the gateway

comments: 2026-03-14 12:15 - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer reported elevated 5xx errors starting ~12:05 UTC. Collected request ids and tenant id. Escalating to SRE.
2026-03-14 12:22 - Liam Chen (SRE): Noted edge-proxy keepalive counts near limits. Pulling connection metrics and upstream memory profiles. Opening hotfix window for connection reaper rule.

2026-03-14 12:40 - Priya Rao (Serving Runtime): Observed growing KV cache size for rwd-3b-v2; memory delta consistent with unbounded cache entries for streaming sessions. Investigating cache eviction not triggering for certain streaming flags.

2026-03-14 12:58 - Liam Chen (SRE): Applied temporary proxy config to reduce keepalive timeout from 120s -> 30s and lowered max idle per-tenant. Error rate reduced from 8% -> 1.7% for affected tenant. Monitoring for regressions.
2026-03-14 13:20 - Aisha Patel (Support): NimbusPayments confirmed degraded experience is improved but asked for root cause and permanent fix timeline.
investigation_notes: Edge proxy was configured with per-tenant idle limits that accidentally used per-worker instead of global per-proxy limiting after the autoscaling rollout on 2026-02-28.

Long-lived streaming sessions from NimbusPayments contained keepalive KEEPALIVE frames that prevented idle detection; combined with per-worker limits this allowed aggregate idle connections to exceed safe bounds.
Serving runtime KV cache eviction relies on explicit session end signals; stalled streaming sessions did not emit those signals leading to unbounded cache growth under sustained load.
Autoscaler scaling logic uses observed latency percentiles and underestimates load when head-of-line blocking occurs at the proxy (requests never reach runtime quickly enough to trigger scale up).
mitigation: Hotfix #1: Reduce keepalive timeout to 30s and decrease max idle connections per-tenant (rolled at 12:58 UTC) — immediate decrease in 5xx rate observed.
Hotfix #2: Enable aggressive proxy connection reaping for connections with no active frames for >8s for streaming endpoints (rolled to canary at 13:10 UTC).
Customer-side recommendation: Shorten streaming session heartbeat interval and emit explicit session end on client disconnects to help runtime KV eviction.
resolution: Partial: Temporary proxy configuration changes and streaming-heartbeat recommendations reduced error rate and stabilized runtime memory. Root-cause chain identified (per-worker pool limits + stalled streaming sessions + autoscaler blind spot). Permanent fixes scheduled.
next_steps: 1) Engineering patch to fix proxy per-worker -> global limit bug (PR prepared, needs review and load testing)
2) Runtime change to add safety TTL on KV cache entries for streaming sessions that auto-evict if no activity for X seconds
3) Autoscaler improvement to incorporate proxy queue depth telemetry as a signal for scale-up
4) Postmortem and runbook updates: add detection rule and alert for keepalive pool saturation and add customer-facing guidance for streaming session best practices
5) Coordinate with NimbusPayments CS for pre-postmortem review and delivery timeline
